risks.note: Management names raw material prices among the factors influencing results of operations, and lists raw material price volatility as a factor that may impact operations and margins. As a specialty chemical converter with an explicit backward-integration programme still in development, input cost moves pass directly into margin.

Future growth is stated to depend on successful execution of capacity expansion, R&D, new product development and backward integration — the Tarapur acrylic emulsion expansion, salicylic acid capacity enhancement and new salicylates, peroxide molecules and critical raw materials. Execution may be affected by capital availability, technology development, regulatory approvals, raw material availability, scale-up and market acceptance. No commissioning date is disclosed for either project.

Capital availability is named as an execution constraint on the growth plan, and the MD&A's own ratio disclosure shows a current ratio of 1.01 with a debt-equity ratio that rose to 2.99 from 2.66 and a debt service coverage ratio of 0.54 — i.e. the company is funding an expansion programme while leverage is increasing.

Revenue is generated from only four product verticals, and performance is stated to depend on demand across paints and coatings, pharmaceuticals, cosmetics, adhesives, construction, textiles, paper, renewable energy and other industrial applications. Domestic and global economic conditions may impact operations and margins.
risks.risk: End-market demand cyclicality and concentration in a narrow product set

risks.note: The Company states the chemical industry is diverse and competitive, with competition driven by product quality, technical capabilities, pricing, manufacturing capacity, customer relationships and supply reliability; it competes across multiple specialty chemical segments rather than holding a single protected niche.

Regulatory requirements are flagged both as a factor that may impact operations and margins and as a potential constraint on project execution (regulatory approvals). Organic peroxides are a hazard-regulated product class, and the Company itself cites regulatory requirements as a barrier-to-entry dynamic in that segment.

The Company supplies international markets and manufactures 20+ peroxide products for global markets. Foreign exchange movements, supply-chain disruptions, geopolitical uncertainties and global competition are named as factors that may impact operations and profitability.

currentContext.expansion: Two named capacity projects are disclosed, both in prose and without a stated rupee quantum or commissioning date. (1) Water-Based Acrylic Emulsions: an expansion at Tarapur, Maharashtra is described as 'currently underway', expected to raise potential production capability from approximately 2,000 tonnes per month to approximately 4,500 tonnes per month upon completion. (2) Salicylic Acid: capacity is approximately 50 tonnes per month today, with planned expansion to approximately 200 tonnes per month, alongside development of downstream salicylates (methyl salicylate and additional salicylates for cosmetics and fragrance applications). Alongside the capacity projects the Company describes a backward-integration programme in Organic Peroxides — two critical peroxide raw materials already developed internally and moving towards pilot trials, expected to support approximately six additional peroxide products — plus an R&D pipeline of new salicylates, peroxide intermediates and other specialised molecules progressing towards pilot and commercial stages, supported by the R&D Centre at Tarapur. The Board's-Report 'Factors affecting our Result of Operation' names the same project set ('the Tarapur acrylic emulsion expansion, Salicylic Acid capacity enhancement and development of new salicylates, peroxide molecules and critical raw materials') and flags that execution may be affected by capital availability, technology development, regulatory approvals, raw material availability, scale-up and market acceptance. The MD notes the Dahej, Gujarat facility showed consistent improvement in throughput, plant operations and capacity utilisation during FY2025-26 while Tarapur maintained stable operating performance. No capex rupee amount, no project cost, no funding plan and no target completion date are disclosed anywhere in this bundle.
